lead.zh-Hans: 从{city}寄来，纸边还给江水留着位置。
lead.en: A little room for the river in this note from {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 我沿着外滩走，把黄浦江边的楼房画成一排小方块。旁边也在画画的旅人看了看，说我的邮包占了半张纸。我问这幅画该叫什么，对方还在想；明天也许能收到一个比画还长的名字。
text.en: I tried drawing the Bund’s riverside buildings as a row of little boxes. A fellow sketcher noticed that my mailbag had somehow taken up half the page. I asked for a title. They are still thinking; tomorrow the title may need more paper than the picture.
Ask the sketcher for a title
Look at the building outlines

lead.zh-Hans: {city}的这张速写，最安静的地方还没画完。
lead.en: The quietest corner of this {city} sketch is unfinished.

text.zh-Hans: 我在豫园看亭阁、山石和池水，想在纸上给它们各留一个角落。画到池水时，铅笔自己先躺下来休息了。我只好把倒影留成一块空白。明天再看，也许这块空白反而最像。
text.en: Pavilions, rocks, ponds: I gave each a corner of my Yuyuan sketch. The pencil lay down for a rest just as I reached the water. Its reflection is still a blank patch. Tomorrow I may decide that was the best part of the drawing.
Talk about the unfinished corner
Keep that patch of blank paper

lead.zh-Hans: {city}的午饭，先在菜单上占几个小圆圈。
lead.en: A few small circles reserve lunch a place in my {city} notebook.

text.zh-Hans: 午饭吃了南翔小笼。薄皮里包着肉馅和汤汁，我等它凉一点，才开始画菜单。先画的几个小笼都太圆，简直像邮包里的纽扣。我给其中一个补上褶子，剩下的明天再认领。
text.en: Lunch was Nanxiang xiaolongbao, thin wrappers holding pork and broth. While they cooled, I began a menu sketch. My first attempts looked suspiciously like spare buttons. One now has pleats. I will sort out the others tomorrow.
Find another menu doodler
Add pleats to the little circles

lead.zh-Hans: {city}的这张菜单，底下那笔尤其认真。
lead.en: One particularly determined underline on today’s menu from {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 今天的生煎有金黄酥脆的底。我画手绘菜单时，在底下描了一条粗线，想把那一点脆也带回去。结果纸背还能看见它，倒像这顿饭自己签了名。明天翻页时要慢一点。
text.en: Today’s shengjian had golden, crisp bases. I drew a firm underline on the menu sketch to remember the crunch. It shows through the paper, as though lunch signed the next page too. I had better turn that page carefully tomorrow.
Give the underline a name
Check the mark on the back

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，那张江边速写真的等到了名字。
lead.en: You wrote, “{reply}.” Our riverside sketch finally has its title.

text.zh-Hans: 上回那位画画的旅人给外滩速写想好了名字：邮包也来散步。我把标题写在背面，对方又添了一笔小小的提手。现在这张纸两面都有事做了。我还空着一个角，准备留给下次见面。
text.en: The other sketcher has a title for our Bund picture: Mailbag Goes for a Walk. I put it on the back, and they added one tiny handle. Both sides of the paper are busy now. There is still a corner left for our next meeting.
Trade another drawing next time
Look at the tiny added handle

lead.en: Two menu sketches from a meal in {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 午饭点了小份的南翔小笼和生煎，一份蒸，一份煎。我和邻座聊起画菜单，先给薄皮的小笼画了圆圈，又给生煎添上粗粗的底线。对方说两张纸像在互相写信。我把它们并排收好，明天看看谁先开口。
text.en: Lunch came in two small portions: steamed xiaolongbao and pan-fried shengjian. I chatted with my neighbour while drawing a menu for each, circles for the thin wrappers and bold lines for the crisp bases. They thought the two sheets looked like pen pals. Tomorrow I will see which writes first.
Talk about the two menus
Compare the two sketches

lead.en: Two menu sketches from a meal in {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 今天尝了小份的南翔小笼和生煎。我先在菜单上描小笼的薄皮，再给生煎的脆底涂深一点。两张纸摆在一起，深浅刚好不同。我在背面各留了一行，等明天的小发现自己过来。
text.en: I tried small portions of xiaolongbao and shengjian today. On one menu I drew the delicate wrappers; on the other I shaded the crisp bases. Side by side, the pages have quite different moods. There is a spare line on each back for whatever I notice tomorrow.
Talk about the two menus
Compare the two sketches
